newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq counts 80 U.S., allied sorties on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Iraq counts 80 U.S., allied sorties on Friday.

text.p: Baghdad said U.S. and allied warplanes had flown 80 sorties over Iraq on Friday, but Iraqi forces were unable to intercept or shoot down any of them.
"Until now our planes and anti-aircraft weapons have not been able to intercept and shoot down any of aggressors' planes," said state television, quoting a military spokesman.

The spokesman said based on information from Iraqi radars, the U.S. and allied warplanes had flown 80 sorties over northern and southern Iraq on Friday from their bases in Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.
Iraqi leaders this week vowed to ignore air exclusion zones declared by the United States, Britain and France over northern and southern Iraq in the aftermath of the 1991 Gulf War.

The United States fired cruise missile at air defence targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday after Baghdad troops helped a Kurdish group seize the northern town of Arbil from a rival faction last Saturday.
Washington and London extended the southern no-fly zone on Wednesday, taking its northern limit to the 33rd parallel, 50 km (30 miles) south of Baghdad.
France said on Thursday its planes would continue policing southern Iraqi skies but would not cross the 32nd parallel, the northern limit of the zone set up in 1992.
A U.S. military official in the Gulf said on Friday allied planes had increased sorties over the extended no-fly zone in southern Iraq and had encountered limited Iraqi ground radar activity.
